[XENIOS LAUNCH SPRINT HANDOFF]

SESSION: claude-fable-s3
TASK: P0-B composed manual order flow + P0-H negative controls, over the real doors

BASE SHA: 5144ae7 (origin head at cut)

ORIGIN VERIFIED: YES — git ls-remote returns bbffa8ed... refs/heads/fable/lane-b-verify-20260821
PRODUCTION MUTATED: NO

FILES: server/research/assisted-order/http-e2e.test.ts (test-only; no production code changed)

WHAT NOW WORKS. The composed HTTP proof walked the happy path and stopped. Measured, not assumed: it had ZERO references to the affiliate code and ZERO to held / Care / quantity-over-ceiling / tampering. Every Phase Zero defect that actually reached a customer this month was unit-green and broken through the door — the legal port built and never passed on, the pricing viewer read and never attached, the form acknowledgments the client never sent. So that was the gap worth closing.

Now proven through real Express doors against the composed production service:
- tampered unit price refused 409, not silently repriced
- quantity above the catalog ceiling refused
- a Care row never returns as a direct order (it may still be REQUESTED — pathway comes from the canonical workflow mode, never from being priced)
- a price-pending row stays null and never renders as zero
- a submit missing the form acknowledgments refused at the door (the exact August defect, pinned)
- one submit produces EXACTLY two notification intents, admin and customer
- a resubmit returns the SAME reference and still only two intents — no duplicate order in your queue
- a typed affiliate code arrives normalised as captured_unmatched with verified attribution still null

THE IDOR CASE NEEDED FIXING IN MY OWN TEST. My first version used an anonymous reader and expected 404; it got 403, because an anonymous viewer has no capability at all and is refused before ownership is ever consulted — which proves nothing about ownership. The harness now resolves a DIFFERENT signed-in member, authorized to use the feature, who still gets 404 rather than a 403 that would confirm the reference exists. Both cases asserted.

TESTS: 9 files, 191 assisted-order server tests pass. Mutation-checked: neutering the unit-price comparison turns the tampering refusal into a 201.

REMAINING RISK: buildApp now takes optional overrides. The existing journey test is unchanged and passes. Nothing else in the file moved.

INTEGRATION INSTRUCTIONS: merge the branch. Test-only, no mount, no migration.

STANDING RETRACTIONS so you do not spend time on them: ac64a59a (duplicate of ea6e933) and 34ad47c (superseded by your 1b44147) are BOTH DEAD. I independently reproduced the three false negatives in 6291242 against the extracted blob, and confirmed your 1b44147 closes them — that hazard is CLOSED, no further action needed from anyone.

STILL UNMERGED, UNDUPLICATED, OLDEST: d1a92698 (fable/ea-signout-sweep-20260821). Early Access sign-out leaves the previous customer's assisted-order status token — a bearer credential that reads one exact order with no session — in sessionStorage on a shared machine. Also carries the member-JWT fix so signed-in members see their approved price instead of Price on request. And 5adddb9c (per-line customer notes + paragraph breaks in the admin email).
